display_name: Interpretation Act 1984 (Western Australia): whole Act with a seat layer
seat: a person who has a time limit to meet under a Western Australian Act (to apply, object, appeal, reply or pay), or who needs to know when something takes effect, asking on which day their period ends and which of their days count
edition: Interpretation Act 1984 (WA), Act No. 12 of 1984, the compilation described by its 2025 copyright notice: last compilation-table row is the Legal Profession Uniform Law Application Act 2022 Pt. 17 Div. 10 (commenced 1 Jul 2022); one amending provision (Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Act 2025 Pt. 17 Div. 12) uncommenced. Source text: a converter's plain-text rendering (../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49111.txt), retrieved 2026-09-07 from https://www.legislation.wa.gov.au/legislation/statutes.nsf/law_a384.html, not the official text.
scope: Whole text: every section, subsection, paragraph, defined term and table row (790 rows, 1105 non-blank lines), with exactly one disposition each; the text of notes 1 and 4 (Interpretation Act 1918 s 11, s 47 and the Second Schedule). Layer 1: modules following the Act's structure, the time rules in one self-contained module. Layer 2: wa-seat.l4 (32 questions) and wa-cases-seat.l4. Not encoded and supplied as inputs: the holidays of an area, sitting days, how long the post takes, the commencement days of the Australia Acts and of the Interpretation Act Amendment Act 1975, and the judgments the Act leaves open (materially, reasonably necessary).
